name: Dashboard Layout with Collapsible Sidebar
description: An app shell where the page itself scrolls: a sticky header that never covers the focused element, the sidebar in its own sticky column from 1024 px and the same sidebar as a drawer below, with the rest of the page inert, a footer that scrolls with the content, and a content column that wide tables can't widen.

tokens.note: Suggested defaults. The project's design tokens and existing components win.

layout.layering: Layers, bottom to top: the page, sticky bars, dropdowns and popovers, toasts, then modals, which make the rest of the page inert. The project's layering scale wins; native <dialog> and the popover attribute use the top layer and need no z-index. The sticky header and the sidebar's column are sticky bars; the drawer is a modal.

positioningContract.page: A grid with the sidebar's column and the main column (minmax(0, 1fr)), at least 100dvh tall, with 100vh as the fallback
positioningContract.sidebar: Sticky at the top, as tall as the window, scrolling inside itself; below 1024 px a fixed drawer over the page
positioningContract.header: Sticky at the top of the main column
positioningContract.content: The main element, in the page's normal flow
positioningContract.footer: At the end of the main column, scrolling with the content

invariants: The page scrolls, not a box inside it, so keyboard scrolling, find in page, and the scroll position after Back work as on any page
scroll-padding-top at the header's height keeps focused elements and link targets clear of the sticky header
The main column is minmax(0, 1fr), so wide content scrolls inside itself instead of widening the page
Nothing is position: fixed apart from the drawer and its backdrop below 1024 px

aiAgentInstructions.summary: Build or extend an app shell: a sidebar, a header, the main area, and a footer. The page itself scrolls; the sidebar's column and the header are sticky, scroll-padding-top keeps focused elements clear of the header, and the footer scrolls with the content. Below 1024 px the same sidebar is a drawer, and the rest of the page is inert while it's open. Build on the project's layout components when it has suitable ones, and on the Sidebar Navigation guide for the sidebar itself. Implement only what the task needs, keep existing APIs, and match the project's styling and tokens. The project's conventions win for styling and visual defaults; if one conflicts with an accessibility or correctness requirement in this guide, ask the user instead of choosing silently. Target WCAG 2.2 AA.
keyFeatures: A page grid where the page scrolls, with a sticky sidebar column and a sticky header, and a footer that scrolls with the content
scroll-padding-top at the header's height, so a focused element is never under it (WCAG 2.2 2.4.11)
A main column of minmax(0, 1fr), so wide tables scroll inside themselves
A skip link, landmarks, and one h1 per page; in a single-page app, focus moves to the new page's h1
Below 1024 px, the same sidebar as a drawer with a Close button, the rest of the page inert while it's open
An account menu and a notifications panel as disclosures, and one polite status region instead of live widgets
implementationSteps: 1. Detect the framework and its version, the styling system, the tokens, the router, and the existing components (projectDetection). If the project already has an app shell or layout components, configure or extend them to meet this guide instead of building others, and keep their APIs.
2. Choose what the task needs: a collapsible sidebar, breadcrumbs, notifications, the account menu. Leave out the rest.
3. Lay out the page grid (layoutModel, frameworkPatterns.pageGrid): the sticky sidebar column and header, scroll-padding-top, and the minmax(0, 1fr) column.
4. Add the skip link, the landmarks, and the page's h1 (accessibility.landmarks).
5. Build the sidebar as the Sidebar Navigation guide says, or extend the project's.
6. Below 1024 px, make the same sidebar a drawer (frameworkPatterns.drawer).
7. Build the header's menus as disclosures (components.Header).
8. Check the result against testingChecklist with a keyboard, a screen reader, a phone, and 200% and 400% zoom, and run the project's existing tests and checks.

SkipLink.description: The page's first focusable element, going to the main area

Sidebar.description: A labelled nav: the sidebar's column from 1024 px, the drawer below

Backdrop.description: Below 1024 px, behind the open drawer; a click closes the drawer

MainColumn.description: The header, the main area, and the footer

Header.description: Sticky: the Menu button below 1024 px, search, notifications, and the account menu

StatusRegion.description: One polite status region, present from the start

Sidebar.description: It's the Sidebar Navigation guide's sidebar: 260 px expanded and 64 px collapsed as suggested defaults, with an 80 px rail with a short label under each icon as an option. In the rail, labels are hidden visually only, so every link keeps its name, and the collapse toggle's name says what it does ("Collapse sidebar", "Expand sidebar").

behavior.savedState: A saved collapsed state is applied before the first paint, by a cookie the server reads or a small inline script, and stored under the app's own prefix, such as acme.sidebar. The rail's styles apply from 1024 px only, so a saved rail never shrinks the drawer.
behavior.widthChange: Collapsing changes the main column's width. Charts and virtualized tables measure their container, so they measure again after the change (a ResizeObserver). Under reduced motion, the width changes at once.
behavior.drawer: Below 1024 px, tablets included, a Menu button in the header (aria-expanded, aria-controls) opens the same sidebar as a drawer over the page. There's no second copy, so no id appears twice. While it's open, everything else is inert (the Modal Dialog guide's model, without a focus-trap library), so focus and screen readers stay in it, and the page behind doesn't scroll. It makes inert only what isn't inert yet, and closing undoes only that, so a part of the page the app made inert stays inert. Focus moves to its Close button. Close ("Close menu"), Escape, a click on the backdrop, and a followed link close it, and focus returns to Menu. If the window gets wider than 1024 px while it's open, it docks, and the inertness it added goes. When the window crosses 1024 px, focus on an element that hides moves to the nearest control that stays, and focus anywhere else stays where it is. Widening hides Menu and Close, so focus on them, the drawer open or closed, moves to the current page's link, or to the first link that shows when that one is in a closed group (a selector list such as [aria-current="page"], a finds whichever comes first in the page, so pick the current one first); narrowing hides the docked sidebar, so focus in it moves to Menu. The same goes for any header control the project hides at a breakpoint. Chromium drops focus from an element a media query hides before a matchMedia listener runs, so the snippet remembers the last focused element and checks whether it still shows. React to a matchMedia change, not to resize events.

Header.description: The header holds the Menu button below 1024 px, then search or the command palette's trigger, notifications, and the account menu.

elements.MenuButton: Below 1024 px: a button named "Menu" with aria-expanded and aria-controls pointing to the sidebar.
elements.AccountMenu: The account menu is a disclosure, as in the Navigation Bar guide: a button with aria-expanded, and a list of links. Sign out is a button that posts a form. It isn't role="menu", which promises arrow-key navigation, and no button here has aria-haspopup.
elements.Notifications: The notifications button's name includes the count ("Notifications, 3 unread"); the badge is hidden from screen readers, and its panel is a disclosure too.

behavior.sticky: position: sticky at the top of the main column, with the project's sticky-bar layer.
behavior.menus: Escape closes an open menu or panel and puts focus back on its button; a click outside closes it.
behavior.announcements: Nothing announces "Sidebar opened": the Menu button's aria-expanded already says it.

Main.description: The main element, the skip link's target: optional breadcrumbs, the page's h1, and the page.

behavior.heading: The page's title is its <h1>, at the start of <main>. Breadcrumbs, when the app has them, are a <nav aria-label="Breadcrumb"> with an ordered list, the current page last with aria-current="page", and the separators hidden from screen readers.
behavior.routeChange: In a single-page app, a route change updates document.title, moves focus to the new page's <h1> (tabindex="-1"), closes the drawer and any open menu, and moves aria-current.
behavior.liveContent: Widgets that refresh don't announce themselves, and the dashboard's grid isn't a live region. One polite status region, in the page from the start, says the results people asked for ("Report exported"); role="alert" is only for urgent errors. Each widget keeps its own loading, empty, and error states, as the Data Table guide does for tables, so each still works on its own.

Footer.description: Optional: links such as Privacy, Terms, and Support, at the end of the main column. It scrolls with the content and is never fixed.

implementationDetails.pageGrid: The page scrolls, not a box inside it. A grid has two columns: the sidebar's, sticky at the top at the window's full height and scrolling inside itself, and the main column, whose header is sticky at its top. The footer sits at the end of the main area and scrolls with the content; it's never fixed. Keyboard scrolling then works without first focusing an area, and so do find in page, links to a section, the scroll position after Back, and phone toolbars that hide while scrolling. scroll-padding-top on the root element, set to the header's height, makes the page scroll focused elements and link targets clear of the header (WCAG 2.2 2.4.11). Checked in Chromium, Firefox, and WebKit: with it, a link focused under the header is scrolled clear (Chromium and Firefox center it, WebKit puts it just below the header); without it, the link stays covered. The main column is minmax(0, 1fr). Grid and flex children default to min-width: auto, so with 1fr a table with many columns or a long line of code widens the page, even inside its own scrolling container (checked in Chromium, Firefox, and WebKit). Wide tables and code blocks scroll inside their own container, as the Data Table guide says; don't hide overflow on the content area, which clips content and focus outlines. Full heights use 100dvh, with 100vh before it for older browsers, so phone toolbars don't hide the bottom.
implementationDetails.landmarks: The sidebar comes first in the page, so the page starts with a skip link to <main id="main" tabindex="-1"> (WCAG 2.4.1). The sidebar is a labelled <nav>, the header a <header>, the content <main>, and the footer a <footer>. The page's title is its <h1>, at the start of <main>. Breadcrumbs, when the app has them, are a <nav aria-label="Breadcrumb"> with an ordered list, the current page last with aria-current="page", and the separators hidden from screen readers. In a single-page app, a route change updates document.title, moves focus to the new page's <h1> (tabindex="-1"), closes the drawer and any open menu, and moves aria-current.
implementationDetails.layering: Layers, bottom to top: the page, sticky bars, dropdowns and popovers, toasts, then modals, which make the rest of the page inert. The project's layering scale wins; native <dialog> and the popover attribute use the top layer and need no z-index. The sticky header and the sidebar's column are sticky bars; the header's panels are dropdowns; the drawer is a modal.
implementationDetails.appearance: Suggested defaults; the project's design and tokens win. The header is 64 px tall. Content padding is 24 to 32 px from 1024 px and 16 px on phones; a maximum width for reading, such as 1400 px, is optional. Text meets 4.5:1, and focus indicators, the current link's marker, and form controls' edges 3:1. Check the project's own colors the same way. Motion is optional: the sidebar's width changes over 200 ms, and the drawer slides in over 250 ms. Under prefers-reduced-motion: reduce, nothing slides.

framework.description: Find the framework, its version, and how existing components are written before writing code.
detectionSteps: Read the project's dependencies (package.json or its equivalent) for the framework and its version, and use the syntax that version supports.
Open two or three existing components to see their file structure, state handling, and naming.
Look for an existing component that already does this job, in the project or in a design system or UI library it uses, and build on it.

stylingSystem.description: Use the styling system the project already uses, and only that one.
detectionSteps: Check the dependencies and config for the styling setup: Tailwind (version 4 keeps its theme in CSS with @theme, version 3 in tailwind.config.*), CSS Modules, Sass, CSS-in-JS, or plain CSS.
See how existing components apply styles and compose class names, for example with cn or clsx.
Check for design documentation: DESIGN.md, a design system package, or Storybook stories for existing components.
adaptationRules: Write styles the way existing components do, and add no new styling library or system.
With plain CSS, use classes in the project's stylesheets instead of inline styles, except for values computed at runtime.
If the setup is unclear or mixed, ask before choosing.

designTokens.description: Use the project's tokens for color, spacing, radius, type, shadows, motion, and layering.
detectionSteps: Find the tokens: CSS custom properties, a Tailwind theme (@theme or config), a theme object, or a tokens file.
Use them instead of this guide's example values; where there are none, match the closest existing components.
Check that the colors you use meet the contrast minimums: 4.5:1 for text, and 3:1 for focus indicators, icons, and control boundaries.

frameworkPatterns.note: Short snippets in plain HTML, CSS, and JavaScript for the parts that are easiest to get wrong; adapt them to the project's framework and its version. The sidebar's own markup, its collapsed rail, and its saved state are in the Sidebar Navigation guide.

drawer.description: Below 1024 px, the same sidebar as a drawer: Menu opens it; everything that isn't inert yet becomes inert while it's open, and closing undoes only that; Close, Escape, and the backdrop close it; and crossing 1024 px either way keeps focus on something that stays.

edgeCases.manyItems: The sidebar's column scrolls on its own, and keeps the current link in view.
edgeCases.shortScreens: Phones in landscape and 400% zoom leave little height, so only the 64 px header sticks; the footer scrolls with the content.
edgeCases.wideContent: Tables and code scroll inside their own container, and the page doesn't scroll sideways at 320 px wide.
edgeCases.secondPanel: A panel of filters or details on the other side follows the same rules: its own column from 1024 px, a drawer below.
edgeCases.noScript: Render the sidebar and the page on the server. Below 1024 px the drawer needs the script, so keep the main sections reachable without it too, such as from the home page.

must: Build on the project's layout and navigation components when they're suitable, and keep their APIs
Let the page scroll, with a sticky header and scroll-padding-top at its height
Use one sidebar for the docked column and the drawer, with the rest of the page inert while the drawer is open
Use the project's framework version, styling system, and tokens, the way existing components do
mustNot: Add a dependency, such as a focus-trap or scroll-lock library, without asking
Fix the header or the footer with position: fixed and pad the content to make room
Hide horizontal overflow on the content area
Make the dashboard's grid, a widget, or a badge a live region
Use role="menu" for the account menu, or put aria-haspopup on disclosure buttons
Use inline styles for static values in a plain-CSS project, or hardcode colors the project has tokens for

testingChecklist: The page itself scrolls; the sidebar's column and the header stick, and the footer scrolls with the content
A link focused under the sticky header is scrolled clear of it (scroll-padding-top at the header's height)
A table or code block wider than the column scrolls inside itself, and the page never scrolls sideways, down to 320 px wide
The page starts with a skip link to the main area, and has one h1, the page's title, at the start of main
Breadcrumbs, if any, are a nav named "Breadcrumb" with the current page last, marked aria-current="page"
Below 1024 px, Menu opens the same sidebar as a drawer with a visible Close button, and focus moves into it

While the drawer is open, the rest of the page is inert and doesn't scroll; Close, Escape, the backdrop, and a followed link close it, focus returns to Menu, and what was inert before it opened stays inert

Crossing 1024 px either way, focus on what hides moves to what stays: from Menu or Close to the current page's link (or the first link that shows, when that one is in a closed group), and from the sidebar to Menu; focus anywhere else stays where it is
The account menu and the notifications panel are disclosures that close on Escape and on a click outside; Sign out is a button
The notifications button's name includes the count, and widgets, badges, and the dashboard's grid aren't live regions
In a single-page app, a route change updates the title and moves focus to the new page's h1
A saved collapsed sidebar applies before the first paint, so the layout doesn't shift on load, and from 1024 px only, so the drawer stays expanded
Under reduced motion, the sidebar and the drawer change without sliding
Styles come from the project's styling system and tokens
